newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude plunges into close on Saudi talk.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude plunges into close on Saudi talk.

text.p: IPE Brent crude plunged into the close to end over $1.50 a barrel weaker as rumours the United States has asked Saudi Arabia to increase output to make up for delayed Iraqi exports prompted a price spiral, brokers said.
"The market was extremely vulnerable. Volumes had become incredibly thin and it managed to make a major break lower," said a broker. "There were just no buyers out there."
Nov Brent slid late to close at the session low of $21.55 a barrel, down $1.53 from Friday's close, as the Saudi talk extended early losses prompted by easing Middle East tension.
But Gulf sources denied the U.S. has asked any oil producer to intervene in the market, adding that Saudi Arabia was sticking to its OPEC quota of 8.0 million barrels per day.
Crude was already on the defensive after the U.S. backed away from missile attacks against Iraq and Baghdad said it would no longer fire at U.S. warplanes enforcing "no-fly" zones.

While President Clinton said Monday the United States sought no confrontation with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, Defense Secretary William Perry warned Saddam to stop deploying anti-aircraft missiles in the extended southern no-fly zone or face the consequences.

Brent was driven to a post-Gulf War peak of $24.39 last Thursday by expectations of further U.S. military action against Iraq. The two-week old rally began when the oil-for-food deal was suspended after Saddam intervened in Kurdish fighting.
Earlier, IPE gas oil fell with Brent but tight stocks in the approach to winter were still lending solid fundamental support.

U.S. Energy Information Agency chief Jay Hakes on Monday warned that U.S. refiners are unlikely to be able to fill heating oil inventories ahead of this winter rapidly enough to avoid a steep price rise.
